steps.title: Independent domains
steps.body: The three synthetic roots use different keys in the KMS. Each domain issued one identity.

steps.title: Available operation
steps.body: Cross Sign lets you select a signing CA and a target CA. The screen states that both private keys must be in the KMS.
steps.note: The certificates were prepared through the API before recording; this demo does not perform the operation on screen.

steps.title: Prepared inventory
steps.body: All three self-signed roots were retained and four additional certificates were created: A → B, B → A, A → C and B → C.

steps.title: Hierarchy view
steps.body: The hierarchy shows each CA certificate as a separate entry under its issuing certificate. The self-signed versions remain roots.

steps.title: Certificates and issuers
steps.body: Entries with the same subject name represent different certificates. The visible parent identifies which root signed each cross-certificate.

steps.title: Key graph
steps.body: The graph groups certificates by key: A and B are joined by a double arrow and both point to C. C has no outgoing links.

steps.title: Partial mesh
steps.body: Only A and B have reciprocal links. C → A and C → B are missing, so this is not a full mesh.

steps.title: Certificate table
steps.body: The table distinguishes certificates by Common Name, CA Issuer and serial number, and also lists the issued identities.

steps.title: B identity
steps.body: Demo-B issued B’s identity. Its details show the validity and the two-certificate chain selected by the interface.

steps.title: Public certificate
steps.body: Certificate PEM displays the public certificate; the identity’s private key is not shown.

steps.title: External validation
steps.body: OpenSSL validated B’s identity from A using A → B as an intermediate, and A’s identity from B using B → A. Before B → A was created, A’s identity did not validate from B when no intermediates were supplied.
steps.note: The observed profile supports validity, usages, subject, algorithm and CA type; controls for the examined policy and name constraint extensions were not observed. The explicit policy test failed.
